subject: Snapshot handback: gating, exit criteria & rollback owners
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Snapshot handback: gating, exit criteria & rollback owners

Team —

We just handed back the latest stability snapshot after the promptset B canary showed a regression on a subset of NLU prompts (attached: eval_snapshot_20260427.csv). Product is asking for a tight decision path so we can either patch and re-promote or roll back. I need the following by EOD today: 

- Proposed gating metrics and numeric thresholds that would trigger an automated pause (and why those thresholds).
- Clear owner for rollback authority (team + on-call contact).
- Minimum acceptance criteria to allow a re-promote (metrics to reach and tests to pass).
- Rough ETA for mitigation (hotfix or model variant promote).

Notes: this is impacting a small but high-sensitivity customer segment (Acme Financial) who reported higher false-positives on transaction classification. Marker: there are three failing buckets — intent drift, hallucination of merchant names, and a latency spike affecting timeouts.

I attached the snapshot CSV and a draft rollback_play.md. Marissa — can you also surface which promptset slices we should gate on vs. smoke tests?

If we don't have alignment, I'll pause the rest of the rollout at 6PM PT and escalate to on-call.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: eval_snapshot_20260427.csv, rollback_play.md

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot handback: gating, exit criteria & rollback owners

On Tue, Apr 28, 2026 at 9:12 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> We just handed back the latest stability snapshot after the promptset B canary showed a regression on a subset of NLU prompts (attached: eval_snapshot_20260427.csv).

Quick analysis (high level):
- Root cause appears to be a tokenization edge-case combined with KV-cache eviction for longer-context flows; that explains the latency spike and the hallucination cases clustered in long receipts.
- We validated on staging that switching to model-v2-quantized reduces the hallucination rate but increases latency ~20ms.

Suggested gating metrics (automated checks):
1) Customer-facing macro F1 drop > 1.5% (rolling 1h) on the tracked NLU benchmark -> pause.
2) Precision (top intent) fall > 2.5% on the finance prompt slice -> pause.
3) 95th pct latency increase > 100ms for requests > 512 tokens -> pause.
4) Any new customer-reported false-positive rate > 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline over a 30-minute window -> immediate pause and page.

Rollback authority recommendation:
- Primary rollback owner: modelserv-team (pager: modelserv-oncall@redwood.com).
- Secondary escalation: SRE lead (markus_klein@redwood.com).

Acceptance criteria to re-promote (minimum):
- All failing promptset slices in eval_snapshot_20260427.csv return to within +/-0.5% of baseline for precision and recall across the sampled set.
- End-to-end smoke tests (sanity prompt suite) pass 100% (no hallucination flags).
- No new customer escalations for 24 hours post-repromote.

ETA for mitigation: 48 hours for a hotfix (tokenizer patch + KV-cache tuning) or 6 hours to flip to the compatible variant (model-v2-quantized) if we accept the latency delta.

I've attached a short KV cache dump/analysis (kv-cache-analysis.txt) and the rollback_play.md is a good start; I can flesh the runbook if we commit to rollback ownership.

— Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachments: kv-cache-analysis.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot handback: gating, exit criteria & rollback owners

On Tue, Apr 28, 2026 at 10:18 AM karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick analysis (high level):
> - Root cause appears to be a tokenization edge-case ...

Thanks for the analysis — I've pulled the failing promptset slices into a matrix and proposed which slices to include in the automated gating scoreboard:

- Finance-intent (high priority) — threshold: precision drop > 2.0% -> gate
- Merchant-entity-extraction (high priority) — threshold: new hallucinations > 0.3% absolute -> gate
- Long-context-invoice (medium) — threshold: 95th pct latency > 80ms -> gate
- Sanity smoke (all) — must pass 100%

I'll own the gating scoreboard and can push a Canary->Pause webhook to the CI if any of the above cross their thresholds. I also suggest we add a short synthetic harness for Acme's top-30 prompts (shared Drive link below).

Plan:
- Today (EOD): agree thresholds & owners — I will wire up the scoreboard for the first gate (finance-intent).
- Tomorrow AM: run a targeted re-eval on the patched tokenizer and the quantized variant (results: by 10AM PT).

Related: Jira PROD-4821 has the tracked test cases; I'll attach the synthetic harness in the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-snapshots).

Marissa Cole
Head of Evals & Quality, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot handback: gating, exit criteria & rollback owners

Thanks for the rapid turnaround. Approve the approach below:

- Grant rollback authority to modelserv-team (primary) and SRE lead (secondary). Modelserv-oncall should be empowered to flip traffic if any gate trips.
- Pause further rollout immediately at 6PM PT if any additional customer reports come in; Grace, take the pause decision if you see any further signal.
- Marissa: own the gating scoreboard and wire the Canary->Pause webhook. Karthik: prioritize the tokenizer hotfix but keep the quantized variant ready as a fallback.
- Require a short standup tomorrow 10AM PT with engineering, product, and SRE; final decision on re-promote or rollback by 5PM PT (2026-04-30T00:00:00Z).

I'll also loop in legal only if the Acme incident escalates to a formal SLA claim. For now, treat this as high-priority operational correctness.

— Markus Klein
VP, Serving & Reliability
